speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to help narrow down the cause, how long has this been happening, and does it wake you up at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury suggests a potential ligament tear or fracture. Did you hear a loud "pop" or snap at the moment of injury, and can you currently make a fist with that hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon rupture).

Based on the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the resting extension of the finger, the injury pattern confirms a rupture of the extensor tendon rather than a flexor tendon or fracture. I will request X-rays to rule out an avulsion fracture.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
